description.narrative:
Media Institute Fojo has applied to the Embassy for funding of MSEK 72 to carry out the "Rwanda Media Programme 2021-25 , Capacity Building and Professionalisation of the Media". The programme will be implemented in partnership with Swedish Radio Media Development Office (SR MDO).
The objective of the contribution is to strengthen the independence, professionalism, and sustainability of key actors in the Rwandan media sector with the aim to increase media diversity and media integrity. This in turn will contribute to increase the population's access to independent, trustworthy, impartial news and information through the media as a platform for citizen's participation and interaction. The programme activities are divided under three Outcome areas, (1) capacity development of targeted media houses on journalistic capacity, management and financial sustainability, (2) capacity development of Rwanda Broadcasting Agency (RBA) in line with the principles of public service media, and (3) strengthening journalist education in targeted universities.
The intervention's total budget is MSEK 78,3, out of which Sida will contribute with MSEK 72 and Swizz Development Cooperation with the part (USD 800 000). Approximately MSEK 32 will be forwarded from Fojo to SR MDO, and about MSEK 14 from Fojo to local implementing partners.

Mediainstitutet Fojo has ansökt om 72 miljoner kronor i stöd för att genomföra insatsen "Rwanda Media Programme 2021-25, Capacity Building and Professionalisation of the Media" mellan mars 2021 och februari 2026. Insatsen genomförs i samarbete med Swedish Radio Media Development Office (SR MDO).
Insatsens mål är att stärka oberoende, professionalism och hållbarhet hos media med syftet att öka en mångfald och integritet i mediasektorn. Detta i sin tur ska bidra till att öka befolkningens tillgång till oberoende och pålitliga nyheter och information genom media och att media på så sätt kan fungera som en plattform för ansvarsutkrävande och medborgerligt deltagande. Programmet är uppdelat i tre resultatområden med specifika mål och aktiviteter, (1) kapacitetsstärkande av utvalda mediahus kring journalistisk kapacitet, management och finansiell hållbarhet, (2) kapacitetsstärkande av Rwanda Broadcasting Agency (RBA) i linje med public service-principer, and (3) stärka journalistutbildningen i utvalda universitet.
Insatsens sammalagda budget är 78,3 miljoner kronor, av vilken Sida finansierar 72 MSEK, och resterande belopp finansieras av den schweitziska ambassaden (800 000 USD). Cirka 32 MSEK kommer vidareförmedlas till SR MDO och ca 14 MSEK till lokala samarbetpartners.

The Overall objective is that the Rwandan people access independent, trustworthy, impartial news and information through the media as a platform for citizens participation and interaction.
The specific objective is strengthening the independence, professionalism, and sustainability of key actors in the Rwandan media sector with the aim to increase media diversity and media integrity.
Outcome 1: Commercial and non-profit media are strengthened to become financially sustainable and to produce and disseminate public interest journalism, reflecting the full composition of society through a balanced presence of women and men, age groups and communities.
Outcome 3: Journalism education institutions have increased skills concerning practical journalism, awareness of gender issues, and are better connected with the Rwandan media and the international journalism community.
The original outcome 2 was formulated as: RBA is strengthened in the process to become an independent, trustworthy and sustainable Public Service Media (PSM) provider according to international journalistic and public service standards. This outcome has been discontinued early 2025 on the initiative of the implementing partner SR MDO. The contribution, hence, remains with the outcome 1 and 3.

title.narrative: Decision on Amendment on Contribution Rwanda Media Programme 2021-2025

description.narrative:
The Mid-Term Evaluation of 2024 (MTE) confirmed that the that Rwanda Media Programme is largely on the right track and effective. Representatives from both public and private media, as well as the universities and womens' organisations, testify that the programme has contributed to an improvement of media in the country and better skills of the media professionals. More than 90 per cent of the respondents from the online survey say that they have improved their skills because of interventions from thre programme.
Outcome 1 - Private media
The MTR found that the RMP has contributed to a stronger private media sector. The media viability programme for the 10 larger private media has yielded tangible results for most of the participating media houses. They have sharpened their editorial profiles and developed clear strategies and visions, and they have increased their understanding of their key audiences. This has also, according to respondents, resulted in increased audiences and also in improved revenues.
The MTR also finds that the cross-cutting gender equality activities have resulted in increased awareness in the newsrooms about gender issues, including gender-based violence, sexual harassment, and the publication of women's perspectives in general. The new industry anti-harassment policy has been developed and endorsed by a wide variety of media houses, and the RMP and the local partners have been part of the development of the pan-African Kigali Declaration on Gender Violence in and through the Media.
Outcome 2 - Public service media
The strong relations between RBA and Swedish Public Service Media (PSM), through SR MDO, and the peer-to-peer support at all organisational levels, have led to several achievements. Results are on the policy level, but also in terms of routines and capacities. Progress can be seen in new leadership skills to a more diversified selection of voices in the RBA news.
Confirmed by the MTE, RBA has moved closer to being a PSM, not only in name. The content production has changed from covering mostly official information from government to a new way of working, where the voices of ordinary citizens are seen as important. RBA continues to deepen its application of public service values, for example by settining targets on giving voices to women, young people and those affected, and not only people in power. It is using insights from audience research to develop content. The shift at RBA has been duly noticed also by colleagues in the private media sector, the MTE notes.
In 2023, the RBAs new 5-year strategy A bridge for citizen engagement in the digital society was finalized with the support of SR MDO. It shows that RBAs direction is both in line with and influenced by SR MDO´s public service development mission within RMP.
An important emerging result is the SR MDO-supported development of a new public service financing model for RBA, moving from private (and government) advertising to a model along the lines of the Swedish and Finnish system of a ring-fenced public service tax.
Outcome 3 - Universities
Progress has been made when it comes to strengthening students in their hands-on practice. Students have gained skills and opportunities to publish their own stories on programme supported student media platforms. Other activities involving guest lecturers, expert mentors, and study tours has had impact in bridging the gap between the media industry and journalism education.
Lecturers at the partner universities have increased their knowledge of new developments in practical journalism. They have also had the chance to expand their regional networks through conference participation and academic exchanges.
The student-led Gender Clubs with the participation of both male and female students have been established at the partner universities.
The curriculum review at one of the universities, Eeast African University of Rwanda, has been finalised.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
